label: agx-ai vLLM Gemma 4 26B-A4B final config, patched image
chat_server_config:
# vllm serve --config for Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT on the RTX 3070 (8 GB) of agx-ai. Benchmarks: README.md
# Built with ../vllm-radeon-vii/repack_gemma4_qat.py (--embed-bits 16 --lm-head-bits 8): all linear weights bit-exact
# from Google's QAT Q4_0 GGUF (int4, group size 32), the lm_head int8 (round-to-nearest, group size 128), the
# embedding fp16 (it is in RAM, see below). 14.97 GiB in total; vLLM reports 4.12 GiB of model memory on the GPU
# with the MTP drafter.
model: /models/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-ct-embed16-head8
served-model-name: google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat
# FP16 like the scales of the Q4_0 GGUF, which BF16 would round.
dtype: float16
# Do not load the vision tower (1.1 GiB).
language-model-only: true
# The experts (11.2 GiB) and the embedding (0.7 GiB) are in pinned RAM, and the GPU reads them directly over PCIe
# (UVA, zero-copy). The MoE kernel reads only the experts that the router selects (8 of 128 per layer, ~765 MiB per
# token), so generation is bound by PCIe 4.0 x16 (~20 GB/s), not by the CPU. The embedding is only looked up.
# cpu-offload-gb is only an upper limit here: the parameters that match cpu-offload-params are offloaded until it is
# reached. Each layer of experts kept on the GPU (408 MiB, i.e. ~15k tokens of context) would remove only 1/30 of
# the PCIe reads per token (not measured).
offload-backend: uva
cpu-offload-gb: 30
cpu-offload-params: [experts, embed_tokens]
# The KV cache below holds 102909 tokens; vLLM needs ~1.05 times the context. Peak 7755 MiB of the 7839 MiB usable
# with a 96000-token prompt and kv-cache-memory-bytes 2850000000, i.e. ~140 MiB less with this setting.
max-model-len: 98304
# Set explicitly instead of gpu-memory-utilization, whose profiling leaves ~1 GiB unused.
kv-cache-memory-bytes: 2700000000
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
# vLLM uses Triton attention for Gemma 4 (head sizes 256 and 512), which supports quantized KV caches.
# int8 with a scale per token and head is the format closest to llama.cpp's q8_0. FP16 would halve the context.
kv-cache-dtype: int8_per_token_head
attention-backend: TRITON_ATTN
# The prefill chunk. Every chunk reads all experts over PCIe, but 4096 was only 8 % faster at 36.5k tokens and
# needs more KV cache for the sliding-window layers: it halves the context.
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
# Full CUDA graphs for decoding with MTP (1 + 2 tokens).
compilation-config: {"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 3, 4]}
# One request at a time, like parallel = 1 of the llama.cpp preset: every sequence needs its own sliding-window KV
# cache, and the experts are read over PCIe per step anyway.
max-num-seqs: 1
# Google's MTP drafter for the QAT model (BF16, 0.8 GB, on the GPU), which shares the KV cache of the main model.
# 2 tokens: +19 % in chat (31.6-32.0 vs 26.6 t/s); 3 tokens was not faster.
speculative-config: {"method": "mtp", "model": "google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized-assistant", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}
enable-prefix-caching: true
# No CPU KV offloading (kv-offloading-size): with the MTP drafter, it stores blocks but never restores an evicted
# conversation for Gemma 4 (without MTP, a 25k-token conversation came back in 0.3 s instead of 25 s). See README.md.
reasoning-parser: gemma4
enable-auto-tool-choice: true
tool-call-parser: gemma4
# Sampling: generation_config.json of the model (temperature 1.0, top-k 64, top-p 0.95), as recommended by Google.

label: agx-ai vLLM Flash-Next final config, final patched image
chat_server_config:
# vllm serve --config for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on the RTX 3070 (8 GB) of agx-ai, with its experts in RAM.
# Benchmarks: README.md. Needs the fixes for UVA weight offloading of ../vllm/vllm.patch (2026-10-13).
# Built with quantize_flash_next_dense.py from albucino/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-FP8PLE: the routed experts in
# Intel's AutoRound int4 and the n-gram table in FP8 as in the source, the Gated DeltaNet, attention and shared
# expert projections and the lm_head in int8 (round-to-nearest, group size 128) instead of BF16, so that the
# weights that stay on the GPU take 5.03 GiB instead of 8.0 GiB.
model: /models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-FP8PLE-dense-int8
served-model-name: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
# Text only: the vision tower would not fit.
language-model-only: true
# The routed experts (58.4 GiB) and the token embedding (1.2 GiB) are in pinned RAM, and the GPU reads them directly
# over PCIe (UVA, zero-copy). The MoE kernel reads only the 10 experts per layer that the router selects (~1.2 GB per
# token), so generation is bound by PCIe 4.0 x16. cpu-offload-gb is only an upper limit here.
# The n-gram table (47.6 GiB in FP8) is in pinned RAM too (engram-config cpu_offload, the default for this model).
# In total ~107 GiB of the container's 128 GiB of RAM are pinned.
offload-backend: uva
cpu-offload-gb: 100
cpu-offload-params: [experts, embed_tokens]
# The KV cache below holds 24041 tokens (~45 KiB per token in BF16; the FP8 cache of this model needs sm_89+).
# Peak 7322 MiB with a 19500-token prompt; with 1.45 GB, a 23500-token prompt ran out of memory.
max-model-len: 20480
kv-cache-memory-bytes: 1100000000
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
# The prefill chunk.
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
# CUDA graphs for single-token decoding: twice as fast as eager mode (15.3 vs 7.4 t/s in chat).
compilation-config: {"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1]}
max-num-seqs: 1
# No MTP: its module (2.6B parameters, an estimated ~1.4 GB on the GPU even with its experts in RAM) does not fit.
enable-prefix-caching: true
reasoning-parser: qwen3
enable-auto-tool-choice: true
tool-call-parser: qwen3_coder
# Sampling: generation_config.json of the model.
